title: Current Mirrors and Biasing
intro: Current sources act as large resistors that cost little headroom, and current mirrors make many accurate copies of one reference current. This chapter (Razavi, Chapter 5) covers basic and cascode mirrors, the active mirror and the five-transistor OTA built on it, and ways to bias each amplifier stage.

items: Basic mirrors: why a fixed gate voltage gives a poorly defined current, copying through a diode-connected device, current ratios and unit-transistor sizing.
Cascode mirrors: removing the channel-length-modulation error, the headroom it costs, and the low-voltage cascode that recovers one $V_{TH}$.
Active mirrors: the five-transistor OTA, its large-signal transfer, gain, and its common-mode and supply behaviour.
Biasing techniques for CS, CG, source-follower and differential stages.

blocks.caption: Basic mirror, including the channel-length-modulation error.

blocks.text: The half-circuit method from the differential-amplifier chapter is used throughout; the OTA pages show where it stops working (the active mirror breaks the symmetry).
